items.body: After nine previous albums and a 25-year career at the forefront of world music, Lucas Santtana is fluent in the many genres of Brazilian music. His new project, Brasiliano , is a musical exploration of the languages of Brazil. With songs sung in Portuguese, French, English, Spanish, Occitan, Cape Verde Creole, and Tupy-Guarani, a Brazilian native language, Santtana has assembled guest lyricists and vocalists representing a range of musical and linguistic influences. The result is a warm and compelling musical treatise on the diverse cultural history of Brazil, expressed through the Brazilian variant of Portuguese, best described as Brasiliano. Returning to his roots, the opening cut and lead single �A hist�ria de nossa l�ngua� features Gilberto Gil, a national treasure with whom Santtana worked early in his career. As the liner notes explain, Brasiliano , the language, is depicted in the song as a feminine character meeting other people (languages) on her travels, tracing the history of the language as an offshoot of Latin, including �Occitan, Celtic, Galician, Portuguese, Mozarabic, and others. The chorus features Indigenous words that are part of everyday Brazilian culture: Itapu�, Ipanema, Maracan�, Capoeira, etc.� This song acts as a sort of abstract for the dissertation to follow. Santtana and Gil call and respond over what has become the composer�s trademark mixture of detailed, layered, human-played instruments, including on this track violins and violas, piano, guitars, mellotron, and synths. Throughout the record, Santtana creates an inviting effect with a contemporary gloss, combined with the warm resonance of wood, drum skins, wire strings, sticks, bows, and voices. The album features a range of styles, from the lively party track �Ver meu povo se abra�ar� to the convincing reggae of the second single, �Que seja um reggae�. With sophisticated songcraft and inspired arrangements, the songs remain inviting and accessible. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Fitting with the theme of the interrelationships among languages, Brasiliano is a celebration of international collaboration. For example, �Independ�ncia� features Karyna Gomes, a singer from Guinea-Bissau; Anglo-French performer Piers Faccini sings �Battre des ailes� accompanied by an appropriately French-sounding accordion; and popular Brazilian singer Flavia Coelho is featured on �Dans le sud feat�. The gentle �Strati di tempo� is the closest to Santtana�s earliest singer/guitarist style, with Italian star Dimartino taking the lead vocals. Brasiliano by Lucas Santtana Language is culture; so too are politics. And with the involvement of Gilberto Gill, who served as Minister of Culture in President Luiz In�cio Lula da Silva�s government and was jailed and exiled for his political affiliations in the 1960s, it is no surprise that this album is overtly political.� For example, on �L�nguas Gerais,� French rapper Oxmo Puccino �speaks about colonization.� Continuing to quote from the liner notes, �Indigenous languages and cultures in South America were buried under European colonization.� Tainara Takua and Oxmo Puccino sing �Cocanha� in Occitan. Their music is part of a movement to prevent this endangered romance language from dying out.� � Like his popular previous recording O Para�so (2023), which was concerned with the environment, Brasiliano is a concept album that explores the role of linguistics in culture. And like on O Para�so , Santtana is never preachy. The high-minded intellectual roots of the project are made palatable by the creative and appealing music assembled to tell the story. It is a message of inclusion, collaboration, and the joy of our shared occupancy in this place and at this time. With many languages, many musical styles, and the artistry of many talented and effective musical partners, Brasiliano is a remarkable achievement in curation and musical skill with a compelling contemporary message. items.body: Photo: Aboubacar Traor� A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The newly released album from Malian musicians Neba Solo and Benego Diakit� is the outcome of a project which began in 2013 when Solo and Diakit�, playing balafon and n'goni respectively, were recorded by Bamako producer Ousmane Ha�dara. He played the result to another record producer, Nick Gold, who was completely taken by what he heard and together they decided to work on the recording to produce a finished album, also enlisting English musician Sonny Johns to help with the production. Gold had previously brought together Ali Farka Tour� and Toumani Diabat� to record what was to become the very successful album In the Heart of the Moon and this was a similar story, Solo and Diakit� also being established Malian musicians coming from different musical backgrounds. Indeed, the balafon and n'goni, though both widely associated with Malian music, are seldom played together. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking , released as a double CD, is very much an album of two halves. The recordings made in 2013 of the two musicians playing together were transformed over time into ensemble arrangements with the addition of other musicians playing strings, mellotron, guitar and percussion, plus overdubbed vocals from Solo and three female singers. These reworked tracks make up the first half of the album. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The opening track, �Djin� Mogo Tiki� begins with a capella backing vocals before Diakit� introduces a repeated riff on the n'goni over which Solo improvises on the balafon while also taking the lead vocal, a pattern which forms the basis of all the tracks, with the augmented instrumentation creating further layers of interest. �Djin� Mogo Tiki� is one of two tracks to have strings added and these sit well, used sparingly to provide short rhythmic motifs, thankfully belying any fears that might be raised by mention of a string arrangement. A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking by Neba Solo & Benego Diakit� The reinvention of these pieces, clearly done with the co-operation of both Solo and Diakit�, may be radical but it has nevertheless been carried out with consideration and musical sensibility. �Yeredon Bali� begins with a few phrases from Solo's balafon, to be joined by Diakit�'s n'goni, some light percussion and hand claps and then more of the female backing vocals, supporting Solo's vocal in the call and response style characteristic of so much Mande music. In this case the vocal content is the only significant addition to the original duo recording, but significant it is because, in the nature of things, once a vocal line is added that becomes the main focus of attention. What makes the format of this album particularly intriguing is that the final six tracks give us the opportunity of hearing the original, unadorned versions of most of the arranged tracks as first recorded by Neba Solo and Benego Diakit�. They are referred to as the �Garden Demos� since they were recorded in a Bamako garden under a mango tree. Without the added vocals the focus shifts to the interplay between the two musicians, and the meaning of the music changes. "Djine Mogo Tiki (Garden Demo excerpt) For example, we are offered two versions of "Djin� Mogo Tiki," first appearing as the album's opening track in its arranged version, then later in the original duo take. Perhaps this has been done to show two sides of the same story, with an awareness too of differences in what audiences are looking for. The arranged tracks, with their instrumental variety and vocal additions, certainly work well and might help give the music wider appeal. But if you are someone who is captivated by listening to fine players engaged in a musical conversation, eavesdropping on the almost telepathic interaction taking place as the two musicians explore the common ground between them, then it's really already there in the earlier Garden Demos, the final six tracks of A Djinn and a Hunter Went Walking .

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑源自2013年马里音乐家Neba Solo（巴拉风琴）与Benego Diakité（恩戈尼琴）的原始二重奏录音，后经制作人Ousmane Haïdara与Nick Gold的长期再制作，加入弦乐、mellotron、吉他、打击乐以及人声和声层，将原本质朴的二重奏拓展为更丰富的合奏编制。专辑分为两个部分，前半部分是对原始录音的再创作，弦乐编排克制而有效，仅以短促的节奏动机点缀。'Djin Mogo Tiki'以无伴奏和声开场，恩戈尼琴的循环riff之上巴拉风琴即兴盘旋；'Yeredon Bali'则采用典型的曼丁哥一问一答式人声结构。作为世界音乐范畴的作品，两件传统马来乐器的罕见组合以及在保留传统骨架基础上引入现代制作手法的方式，是其值得关注的特色。

items.body:
How do you celebrate 50 years of music by a band that blazed trails for the charged, hypnotic pizzica sound, breaking it out of its homeland in southern Italy? How do you look afresh at a sound that�s changed and broadened its appeal without ever abandoning its roots as a new generation took over the instruments? It�s a challenge, but what Canzionere Grecanico Salentino (CGS) have done is reframe some of the pieces from those earlier decades through the lens of those playing and singing the songs now.
The brainchild of Rina and Daniele Durante, early CGS avidly proudly staked out its territory as champions of an almost forgotten culture. In the hands of their son, fiddler/frame drummer and singer Mauro Durante, the original vision has gone global (he also has a successful duo with guitarist Justin Adams) and they�ve become a major name in world music for their energy and outstanding musicality. They�ve made people in so many countries believe in the pizzica. One big milestone acceptance came with working alongside the celebrated pianist Ludovico Einaudi on his
Taranta
project in 2014, which gave them an even wider reach and boosted them even high. Very aptly, a remix and remastering of the �Taranta� track with him is included.
In a world that loves to dance, this is dance music with depth and power that explodes out of the speakers. It honors the material from the past while keeping its eyes firmly fixed on the future, clasping hands across the generations to celebrate the band and its lauded history.
Il Mito
(The Myth) pays homage without ever being slavish. There�s a real, urgent energy to the music-making here.
The title cut was written by the older Durantes, a cornerstone of CGS�s early repertoire and a reflection on life in their part of Italy. Roberto Licci comes to sing with his son Emanuele. Early vocalist Rossella Pinto reprises her role on �Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare.� Yet this isn�t all hearkening to the past. The sounds have taken on new colors and arrangements as younger fingers play them. It�s still mostly acoustic, with a few electric touches like a synth bass to round out the sound.
This is still completely Italian music, the enveloping, dry sound of pizzica, something that�s evolved over the last half-century, moving from a regional to a global stage. The band, and their compositions, deserve the party, but it begs the question:
Where will all this be in another 50 years?

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Canzionere Grecanico Salentino（CGS）为庆祝乐队成立50周年而作，名为《Il Mito》（神话）。CGS是意大利南部萨伦托地区pizzica音乐的先驱团体，最初由Rina和Daniele Durante夫妇创建，如今由其子小提琴家兼歌手Mauro Durante接手，将这一源自本土、几近被遗忘的传统音乐推向世界舞台。专辑通过当下成员的演奏和演唱视角重新诠释过去数十年的作品，保留原曲根基的同时融入新的编排与色彩。父亲辈创作的标题曲由Roberto Licci与其子Emanuele共同演唱，早期歌手Rossella Pinto也在《Lu Rusciu De Lu Mare》中回归。整体以原声乐器为主，辅以合成贝斯等少量电声元素。专辑还收录了2014年与钢琴家Ludovico Einaudi合作的Taranta项目重混版本，展现了pizzica音乐从地方走向全球的演变路径。

items.body:
Photo: Claudia de Ventura
Crete�s Stelios Petrakis is at the peak of players of his island�s best-known traditional instrument, the Cretan lyra, a small pear-shaped fiddle held vertically on the knee. Its three bowed strings are stopped by the fingernails of the non-bowing hand rather than being pressed to the fingerboard. Its sound hovers on the enticing edge between fundamental and harmonics.
Petrakis is also a leading luthier, making the lyras and the other instruments he plays, including the traditional metal-strung lute laouto, and in conjunction with Ross Daly he�s developed and plays a range of lyras with ringing sympathetic strings.
True to its title, this an album of his lyra, and laouto, with a panoply of other traditional instruments played by musicians of equal stature to Petrakis, in music of rich lyricism, in melody and texture.
�Astro Sti Gaza� (�Star in Gaza�), a wish for peace written by Petrakis with lyrics by his brother Yannis Petrakis, opens the album. At first a string drone, then Petrakis�s laouto and lyra, Ma�lle Duchemin�s harp, Pavlos Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the percussion of Iranian Bijan Chemirani, who plays frame and flask hand-drums on most tracks. The dark, sinuous instrumental line is tracked by the husky vocal of Giorgis Xylouris, who sings on three tracks, the other six being instrumental. �Nathenas,� a traditional Cretan song in asymmetric rhythms, has a powerful ensemble of lyra, laouto, frame-drum, stick-hit davul, topped out by Breton Sylvain Barou�s reeds and Armenian shvi whistle.
�Anglianico,� a stately melody composed by Petrakis, has the tremolo mandolins of Valencian musician Efr�n L�pez and Michalis Kontaxakis in an elegant almost orchestral sound with lyra, guitars (Antonis Voumvoulakis and Samuel Mele), Spyropoulos�s double bass, and the accordion of Mattia Marco Gregoriadis on whose improvisation the tarantella-like �Pukan� is based.
Chemirani is particularly featured on his composition �Panj Pol,� a short finger-rippling, slapping solo on zarb flask-drum whose rhythm is the foundation for the song that it breaks into, �Agrilos,� by Petrakis with lyrics by brother Yannis celebrating the wine-producing district of Crete where they grew up. It develops into a big sound of massed instruments, with a break on frame-drum and Sakir Oran Uygan�s big double-headed davul drum before a surge of squealing tulum bagpipe and other wind instruments from Barou.
�Evlerin �n� Mersin,� a traditional tune from Asia Minor, has a march-like feel, beginning with keening lyra over a slow, inexorable drum pulse, building to soaring epic as more instruments join, peaking with Barou�s zurnas. �Muixeranga,� again with a steady, imposing pulse, is an anthemic tune played in Valencia during the Muixeranga, the traditional building of excitingly high pyramidal human towers in which the big and strong form the bottom layers and the youngest and lightest clamber up to form the topmost. Petrakis intends the track as a message of support to Valencia following the climate-change-driven floods of 2024.
Preluded and accompanied by ringing 3/4 time arpeggiating plucked strings and percussion, with the melody played on lyra, the source of �Nothing Else Matters,� is unexpected: it�s a beautiful version, evocative of memory and perhaps sadness, of a Metallica number.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以克里特岛的标志性乐器里拉琴（lyra）和鲁特琴（laouto）为核心，Petrakis既是顶尖演奏家也是制琴师，与Ross Daly共同开发了带共鸣弦的里拉琴扩展型号。专辑跨越多重文化边界，汇聚了来自伊朗的Bijan Chemirani演奏zarb手鼓、布列塔尼的Sylvain Barou演奏管乐与簧片、瓦伦西亚的Efrén López演奏颤音曼陀林，以及亚美尼亚shvi哨笛和土耳其zurna双管簧乐器等。曲目既有传统克里特民歌与非对称节奏，也有Petrakis原创的庄严旋律，更有为加沙和平祈愿而作的歌曲。制作上将地中海、近东和亚美尼亚传统声响编织成层次丰富的器乐织体，同时保留各文化的音色特质。整体呈现出深厚的传统根基与开放的文化对话，在世界音乐范畴中具有相当的艺术深度和融合广度。

items.body: Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka I n the High Middle Ages, Hildegard of Bingen said that �The truly holy person welcomes all that is earthly.� William Blake declared in The Marriage of Heaven and Hell (1790) that �Exuberance is beauty.� In 1855, Walt Whitman published the poem �Song Of Myself, 51� in Leaves of Grass , which contains the famous line �I am large, I contain multitudes.� I�m just skimming the surface of mystical experience, of those struck by wonder and an all-encompassing insight into how people fit into the �grand scheme of things.� At some point on this trajectory, the boundary between the religious and the secular breaks down and simply being human becomes the ultimate wow. Which brings us to Polish artist Maria Ka�s latest album Di Mashin . Ka found that her family had Jewish roots, a discovery that led her to an immersion in Jewish studies and the Yiddish language. As on 2023�s Der Hemshekh , she unreels original songs written in Yiddish, embracing a politically active feminism and a committed meta-universality. Her musical vision is fragrantly mystical, and she presents us with a whole Yiddish cosmos. While not sharing the same type of musical style, Ka reminds me of John Zorn�s aesthetic of mixing the grotesque and the sacred into Jewish experimental music. She also reminds me of the woman on the phone sampled on Wally Brill�s Jewish cantorial electronica album The Covenant (2007), who confesses she can�t sleep after hearing someone in a bar talking about the Book of Ezekiel and being haunted by the vision of Jews arriving from a future space-time. She sees that we are all suspended in webs of relationships. She is also deeply aware of how we are subject to larger social forces and structures � which sometimes must be met with radical action -- that are the machinery of life. There is a heavy dose of electro and punkish attitude spinning through her musical universe. Ostensibly, the album is divided between electronic and rock tracks, but there is a consistency to the sound that is united in loopy joy. At its best, Di Mashin is sly and sexy. Opening track �Alef � Tsentauri Disko� finds Ka in the city, musing on the seaside, wriggling like a snake at night, and watching Gdańsk wake up. �I often Dream about Cosmos, about the Land above the Earth / overhead / Alef Centauri Jewish disco!� she sings, set to a thumping urban electro grind. (See video below) Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �Vos iz dos?� is a standout, more in the �rock� vein, with Ka howling a debate over the Yiddish language itself. Perhaps it is based in a critique that she received, as she starts with What is this? Maria, what is this? I constantly hear it, it has not finished You speak no Yiddish!/ It�s so easy! Your language is incorrect, mistaken is your speech and dialect! � Given that Ka is producing new modern songs in Yiddish, there is something disarming in acknowledging the tension over who might claim ownership of language itself. Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka �SuperNove� might remind listeners of Jacob wrestling with God, if that battle was done to an �80s new wave beat. Ka has visions of the past, the Old World and old demons, and she fights a ghost that rises to block her way: � I fought him with Strength, punched him with my both hands�I triumphed over him! I myself � I did triumph over him! � And after that victory, � it�s a great Surprise � the Past melted in the Cosmic Blast! � Ka also seems to be challenging herself, pointing in new directions. �Di Kosmish motorn (Cosmic engines)� brought to mind the former Warsaw Village Band�s blues-influenced singer Maja Kleszcz. Depeche Mode�s (fronted by Dave Gahan, of Jewish ancestry) forays into fusing electronica with blues might be another touchpoint. Hearing the cosmic engines like a modern day Pythagoras, she is awestruck by hearing the cosmic engines in her head. �Dos geverk (The mechanism)� offers some grinding guitars to convey the constant motion of the daily rat race � echoed later on by the title track, �Di Mashin (The Machine),� which peels back the layers of society to reveal the incessant obsession for money. The music of �The Machine� is hyperspeed cabaret, close to madness. The system demands more money � but she indicates that she is a spanner in the works, working to bring it down: � I watch the machine�s death / Full and steadily red is my hand in the end. � Di Mashin ?? ?????? by Maria Ka Feminist politics come to the fore on �Ikh bin a froy (I am a woman),� and Ka reminds me a bit of the divine Ms. H of Bingen chanting over a motoric beat. She refuses to be hemmed in by structures, signaling that the Forest is her home, the stars her friends; �I wake up every day / and new scroll create.� Album closer �Di milkhome� (War)� is more future blues, transposing war, empty shipyards, and advice from her mother that all miseries will end and freedom will navigate the turmoil �like huge ships at Sea.� Di Mashin is possessed by such a singular offbeat vision and personal mythology that I wonder where Maria Ka will take her Yiddishfuturism next�Perhaps beyond our solar system, grooving on an interstellar plane with her band wriggling like snakes. Find the artist online. Further listening: Maria Ka - Der Hemshekh Warsaw Village Band & Bassałyki - Sploty WoWaKin - Kraj za miastem

items._cn_summary: 波兰艺术家Maria Ka在《Di Mashin》中以意第绪语演唱原创歌曲，融合电子节拍与朋克态度，构建出带有神秘主义色彩的犹太音乐宇宙。乐评将其美学与John Zorn的怪诞与神圣并置的实验路线相类比，强调作品在电子与摇滚轨道之间保持了loopy joy的一致性。开场曲《Alef Tsentauri Disko》以城市电子研磨节拍为底，歌曲主题涉及对意第绪语本身的辩论与女性主义政治表达。专辑呈现了一种跨越宗教与世俗边界的元普世性视角，将语言复兴、文化寻根与实验声响结合，整体定位介于独立小厂牌的世界音乐实验与电子跨界之间。

items.body: sMiLes by Jowee Omicil B orn in Montreal, Haitian-Canadian musician-composer Jowee Omicil plays a fabulous variety of saxophones, clarinets, trumpets, flutes, piano, and keyboards. He came of age in the choral milieu of his father�s Montreal congregation, studied saxophone and music education at Berklee, and gleaned much from engagement with figures including Wyclef Jean, Tony Allen, Ibrahim Maalouf, Roy Hargrove, Kenny Garrett, Pharoah Sanders, Branford Marsalis, and Marcus Miller among others. Over the course of 2025, Omicil released sMiLes one song per month, each accompanied by a philosophizing podcast. The album opens with a striking reinterpretation of singer and Civil Rights activist Abbey Lincoln�s �Throw It Away,� whose message Omicil invokes in his voiceover, an expression of kinship in creative philosophical outlook. (For good measure, Omicil revisits the title on a distinctive �Throw it Away - FuLL oF LoVe Remix.�) Lincoln�s own 2007 rendition on Abbey Sings (Verve) offers critical context, itself worth a comparative audition for the original melody and the contemplative character of her lyrics. Throw it away, throw it away Give your love, live your life, each and every day And keep your hand wide open, let the sun shine through, Because you can never lose a thing, if it belongs to you. In less accomplished hands, the quirky sampling, effects, instrumentation, and wide-ranging, scruffy, sonic bricolage of sMiLes could make for one muddy m�lange. But no danger lies here in Jowee�s paradoxical, provocative, sound-shifting extended groove. Omicil's voice and sax blend almost imperceptibly in �SOeuR FeLiX AKA BeeHive.� In �Trip to GHanA,� polyrhythm meets wah-tone high-life guitar, cackly sax, and wordless vocalise. sMiLes by Jowee Omicil sMiLes by Jowee Omicil Feat. Mawuena Kodjovi Other titles transport the listener to Haiti, Morocco, Cape Verde, Jupiter, and Mali. �LeTTre Du MALi PouR JonaTHan� is a meditative, revelatory piano solo nearly ten minutes in length. sMiLes by Jowee Omicil sMiLes may invoke the free-blowing spirit of Miles (as on the sound-effected �MiLes ConvoY�), but there is no anxiety of influence here. Far from a rote genuflection to musical antecedents, the prevailing voice throughout is purely Omicil�s. As he counsels, �trust the note.� "Seek for the sound that is within you and the [instrument] will drive you to your destination� the singularity of sound is what I have always been searching for, the sound that comes from the heart, the sound that maybe, perhaps, is only heard in nature, this is what we are looking for when we are talking about sound� deep down, heartfelt uniqueness, always connected with the spirits�" - Jowee Omicil In accord with his music education formation, Omicil also leads music workshops through his BasH! AkademY, �a close-knit setting embracing spontaneity, authenticity, and shared growth,� which in 2025 included �a nomadic music experience traveling the world� to Mindelo, Cabo Verde. In 2026 Omicil will perform in New York, Canada, Martinique, France, Germany, Austria, Poland, Romania, the UK, and an African tour in the planning stage.

items._cn_summary: 海地裔加拿大音乐家Jowee Omicil的专辑以每月一首的形式在2025年逐月发行，每首配以哲学播客。专辑以对民权活动家Abbey Lincoln《Throw It Away》的重新诠释开篇，融合采样、音效与多样化器乐编排。从蒙特利尔成长经历到与多位国际音乐家的合作，Omicil的音乐跨越海地、摩洛哥、佛得角、加纳、马里等地文化背景，作品包含近十分钟的冥想性钢琴独奏，以及将人声与萨克斯无缝融合的实验性曲目。评论强调其声音的'奇异拼贴'特质避免了混乱，体现出对自由即兴精神的继承——受Miles Davis影响却不拘泥于模仿，而是以'信任音符'为创作哲学，探寻发自内心的独特声响。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — 3.5 stars really!!!Sole album from this Flemish jazz-rock band (for lack of a better description) that veered between Zappa-type of rock and Canterbury (Cos & Supersister-type) and shared their sax player with Mad Curry. the band took some of its roots from The Pebbles - the first Belgian pop band to achieve international attention, along with Wallace Collection and landed a record contract with a French label. Maybe their music was so ambitious that their album was called Volume 1, hoping that... If you thought Mad Curry was strange (as in (typically Belgian), wait to get a load of this group. Throw in the ingredients above, add a twist of more conventional prog, a dash of music hall type of stuff (almost big-band), a pinch of brass-rock, and you've git something that will make you WTF'ing, but will keep you rivetted to your speakers. These guys must've had an amazing substance dealers. ;-))))Opening on the bilingual (Fr/En) goofy Brother, you're thrown into the deep side of the pool, and they won't let you climb back out over the ledge. Clearly the album's staple is the 11-mins Some Reason, with some strait-jazz soloing from the brass players. Cool Day is anything but that, because it drives you wild with its multiple changes. the flipside offers more of the same madness, but it's too bad for the drum solo in the 9-mins Hurry Up that overstays its welcome and the spoken vocals of the closing Honeybee.Just like Mad Curry's self-titled album, this is a tad too weird to have become a real classic, even for a long-lost unearthed gem. Too bad, they had enough chops and ideas to get you tripping on another 40-mins psych flight.Probably too ambitious a work for the times, the band would follow a disastrous collaboration with a trio of Dutch soul-singers (Heart Of Soul), and the results are out of bounds for this site. Definitely worth the detour and have you haed washed with Shampoo to counter the hair-spikes you'd gave after listening to this album.
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1972年比利时弗兰德地区爵士摇滚乐团的唯一专辑，融合了Zappa式摇滚与Canterbury场景的怪诞气质，铜管乐手同时服务于Mad Curry乐队。专辑开场即以双语演唱将听者抛入荒诞情境，11分钟的核心曲目Some Reason展现了纯正的爵士铜管独奏，Cool Day则以频繁的变拍与情绪转折制造张力。后半部分的Hurry Up鼓独奏略显冗长，收尾的Honeybee采用念白式人声。这张作品试图将传统爵士摇滚与音乐厅风格、铜管摇滚融合，野心远超当时的市场接受度，因此未能成为经典。乐评认为其创意丰富但过于怪异，作为被遗忘的遗珠仍值得挖掘。

items.body: Patrick Clarke reports from France's superb New Trad Fest, where the psychedelic potential of traditional music is on full display, and rounds up essential new folk releases, from euphoric Occitan minimalism to Sicilian worksongs combined with ferocious noise All photos by Titouan Massé Beneath the church of Saint-Aignan is a crypt, once an ancient promontory. Stumbling upon it while wandering on the first of my five days in this small and pretty town in the Loire valley, I’m drawn back to it on three more occasions after that so I can stare more at the walls. The chapels feature frescoes depicting, at various points, Saint Giles, Charlemagne, Jesus Christ and Mary. Though the oldest sections date back as far as the 12th... items._cn_summary: 本文记述了作者参加法国新传统音乐节（New Trad Fest）的见闻，并以此为线索梳理了多张值得关注的传统音乐新发行作品。文章重点关注传统音乐中被忽视的实验性一面，涵盖奥克西坦地区的极简主义民谣、西西里劳动歌谣与暴力噪音的碰撞等多种跨界尝试。作者将法国乡间小镇新传统音乐节呈现的psychedelic传统音乐与教堂地窖中古老的12世纪壁画相类比，暗示古老与前卫之间存在一条隐秘的脉络。整体内容偏向现场见闻与文化随笔，作品推荐只是点缀，正文过短无法深入评价具体唱片。但其关注的传统音乐与实验噪音及psychedelic的融合方向，与实验及世界音乐交叉领域密切相关。

items.body: Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians8 languagesFrom Wikipedia, the free encyclopediaAssociation for the Advancement of Creative MusiciansAbbreviationAACMPredecessorExperimental BandFormationMay 1965FounderMuhal Richard AbramsJodie ChristianSteve McCallPhil CohranTypeNon-profit organizationPurposeSupport and encourage jazz performers, composers and educatorsLocationChicago, IllinoisRegion servedU.S.Official languageEnglishKey peopleHenry ThreadgillAnthony BraxtonRoscoe MitchellAffiliationsBlack Artists GroupEndowmentMacArthur FoundationWebsiteaacmchicago.orgThe Association for the Advancement of Creative Musicians (AACM) is an American nonprofit organization, founded in 1965 in Chicago by pianist Muhal Richard Abrams, pianist Jodie Christian, drummer Steve McCall, and composer Phil Cohran.[1] The AACM is devoted "to nurturing, performing, and recording serious, original music," according to its charter. It supports and encourages jazz performers, composers and educators. Although founded in the jazz tradition, the group's outreach and influence has, according to Larry Blumenfeld, "touched nearly all corners of modern music."[2] Per the AACM, it "pays homage to the diverse styles of expression within the body of Black Music in the USA, Africa and throughout the world."[3]BackgroundeditBy the 1960s, jazz music was losing ground to rock music, and the founders of the AACM felt that a proactive group of musicians would add creativity and outlet for new music.[4] The AACM was formed in May 1965 by a group of African-American musicians in Chicago centered on pianist Muhal Richard Abrams, who had organized the Experimental Band since 1961.[5] The musicians were generally steadfast in their commitment to their music, despite a lack of performance venues and sometimes indifferent audiences. From 1969 the AACM organised a music education program for inner-city youths.[6] In the 1960s and 1970s AACM members were among the most important and innovative in all of jazz, though the AACM's contemporary influence has waned some in recent years. Many AACM members have recorded widely: in the early days on the Delmark Records Avant Garde Jazz series and later on the Black Saint/Soul Note and India Navigation labels, and to a lesser extent on the Arista Records and ECM labels.[7]The musical endeavors of members of the AACM often include an adventurous mixing of avant-garde jazz, classical, and world music. The AACM also ran a school, The AACM School of Music, with classes in all areas taught by members of the AACM. The AACM also had a strong relationship with an influential sister organization, the Black Artists Group (BAG) of St. Louis, Missouri.[8] The AACM has received aid from the MacArthur Foundation and has a strong relationship with Columbia College. A Power Stronger Than Itself: The AACM and American Experimental Music by AACM member George E. Lewis, which documents the AACM's history, has been published by the University of Chicago Press (May 2008).[9]In 2015, a 50-year retrospective exhibition of art, music and group-related artifacts, entitled, "Free at First", was held at the DuSable Museum of African American History.[4]MusiceditThe AACM has been on the forefront of the avant-garde since its inception in 1965. Anthony Braxton, Henry Threadgill, and the Art Ensemble of Chicago pushed the boundaries of jazz and challenged the avant-garde classical movement led by John Cage. Concerts were heavily improvised, and many AACM members created scores that blended music, geometry, painting, and ciphers to be interpreted by the performers live. The AACM was part of an artistic movement on the South Side of Chicago that included AFRICobra (African Commune of Bad Relevant Artists) and other collectives.[10] In the third decade of the 21st century, AACM members continue to produce vibrant avant-garde jazz and jazz-influenced music in Chicago and elsewhere.[citation needed]Membersedit(some deceased; largely complete through at least early 2026) [11] [12]Muhal Richard Abrams[5]Peggy AbramsSoji AdebayoWillel Afi-FiAjaramu Joseph SheltonDee AlexanderMartin AlexanderLeon Q. items._cn_summary: 本文并非针对某张具体专辑的乐评，而是对AACM（创造性音乐家发展协会）的机构性介绍。该组织由穆哈尔·理查德·艾布拉姆斯等人于1965年在芝加哥创立，旨在为爵士演奏家、作曲家和教育者提供创作与演出平台。AACM成员在六七十年代是自由爵士与先锋爵士领域最具创新性的力量之一，其音乐实践常融合先锋爵士、古典与世界音乐元素。早期作品多由Delmark Avant Garde Jazz系列发行，后扩展至Black Saint、Soul Note、India Navigation等小众厂牌。AACM还曾创办音乐学校，为市中心青年提供教育项目，并与圣路易斯的姊妹组织BAG保持密切联系。文章末尾提及了一张专辑名《A Power Stronger Than》，但正文未提供任何关于该专辑音乐内容、演奏风格或录音细节的描述。

items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非传统意义上的乐评，而是芝加哥艺术乐团（Art Ensemble Of Chicago）1969年专辑《A Jackson In Your House》自法国BYG Actuel厂牌首发以来、跨越五十余年的全球各版本唱片目录辑录。内容列举了1969年至2025年间在法国、日本、德国、西班牙、英国、希腊、意大利、美国等多个国家发行的LP、CD、数字版本及其厂牌编号、版本特征如Gatefold折套、180g压盘、橙色彩胶、限量复刻等。作为AACM（黑人音乐家进步协会）成员的核心创作，该专辑代表了自由爵士与即兴实验的高峰，是欧洲前卫厂牌与美国地下先锋力量合作的重要历史见证。对于版本收藏者而言信息价值极高，但缺乏对音乐本身的聆听分析与美学讨论。

items._cn_summary: Don Cherry 1969 年于巴黎 Studio Saravah 录制的双 LP 套装《Mu》由 BYG Actuel 厂牌发行，跨越至 1971 年才正式面世。Cherry 在此作中以口袋小号为核心，辅以钢琴、印度与竹制长笛、人声、铃铛与打击乐器，展现其标志性的世界音乐语汇。从曲目编排来看，《Mu》采用连续拼贴式结构，如《Total Vibration》分作两部呈现、《The Mysticism Of My Sound》与《Psycho Drama》均以 medley 形式串联多个主题片段，段落之间呼应即兴与自发作曲的概念。贝斯手 Ed Blackwell 的鼓击与敲击为整体提供流动的节奏骨架，而 Dollar Brand、Albert Heath 等合作乐手的动机被明确标注为主题来源，体现 Cherry 将多元文化音乐家编织进同一框架的思路。作为 BYG Actuel 系列的作品，专辑延续了欧洲厂牌对 1960 年代末自由即兴的开放态度，是 Cherry 探索环球精神爵士时期的重要文献。

items._cn_summary: 这是Don Cherry于1969年在巴黎Studio Saravah录制的专辑，由法国独立厂牌BYG Actuel发行。Cherry在小号之外还演奏口袋小号、钢琴、印度与竹制长笛，并将所有曲目亲自编曲。打击乐手Ed Blackwell以自由节奏与Cherry的世界音乐理念相呼应，作品跨越自由爵士与灵性爵士的边界，融合非西方音阶与冥想式氛围。BYG Actuel是欧洲前卫爵士的重要厂牌，曾推出多张具有实验精神的自由爵士录音。整张专辑延续了Cherry在全球探索中的东方转向，以简约的器乐组合拓展即兴的深度与广度。

items._cn_summary: 法国钢琴家François Tusques 1971年在巴黎录制的这张专辑，是欧洲自由爵士与政治宣言结合的代表作。曲目名称如《进步力量》《反动力量》《帝国主义是纸老虎》《资产阶级必将在利己主义的冰水中溺亡》等，直接呼应当时法国毛主义思潮，Erika Huggins（黑豹党成员）撰写了内页导言。音乐上采用Tusques擅长的弓拉吉他、锯琴、钢琴、马拉卡斯等多重非传统演奏方式，与Steve Potts的高音萨克斯、Alan Silva的大提琴、Alan Shorter的小号、Sunny Murray的自由鼓击相互碰撞，形成密集的集体即兴对话。Shandar厂牌由Daniel Caux和Marcel Duchamp共同创立，专为实验音乐发行，1973年由RCA在日本再版。此文实为唱片信息整理而非乐评。

items.body: Review by Finnforest — Venti di Cambiamento About fifteen years and three albums into their band history, my perception is that Il Bacio DellaMedusa were ready to try some new things with their fourth studio album, Seme. It certainlydoes feel like a departure from the sound established on their first three albums, which were atrilogy I believe. On this one, they are throwing open the floodgate of ideas and trying whateverthey fancy. The resulting album is likely to be divisive among some fans, but I loved it. Here theyare moving a bit away from the classic progressive rock focus with its many adornments, and they aredabbling with hard rock, folk, fusion, electronic, and all in a noticeably more songs-basedapproach. It's still RPI for sure, but it's been freed up from past expectation with an eye towardtheir future. While I don't typically do track-by-track reviews, this album has so many uniquechange-ups that I feel it's warranted this time.The opening chaos of the title track puts one on notice that this is not IBDM repeating theiracclaimed second album. This is notice that you're getting onto a rollercoaster. Heavy as hell withgnarly metalish hooks and an angry System of a Down vibe, only Eva's sax part sounds familiar earlyon. Great opener that blows the cobwebs from your ears. "La Sonda" is a huge downshift that evokesthe gorgeous days of big-hearted Italian pop, full of beautiful melody, romantic vocals, playfulMoog, and flute. "5 e 1/4. Fuori dalla Finestra il Tempo � Dispari" is a frantic run at heavyfusion, wild, right there with the many Italian fusion bands ala Rocky's Filj or Altare Thotemicoand with the ending turning to a lovely Petrini piano part and Cecchini vocal. Smooth as velvet butalways with great drama. "Sveglia!!!" is a playful country-tinged romp that would make greatsoundtrack for an episode of "Fallout." After an epic guitar solo from Simone Brozzetti, we move tothe first of the experiments with electronic drum and synth treatments in "Animatronica Platonica,"a super cool background with an exterior carried primarily by Cecchini and Brozzetti. The 9-minute "Sudamerica" is quite a centerpiece and another new direction on this adventure of analbum. A slow-paced, building-up track with tabla drumming, laid-back saxophone, and acousticguitars all patiently building to Cecchini's climactic vocal. It serves as a lovely respite in themiddle of this chaotic album. Back to a short and fun throwback interlude, "Uthopia? Il Non Luogo,"which could have been on Abacab. "Il Sentiero Di Luce" is a dash of songs-based "normalcy" if youwill, a bit heavy, a bit folky, overall conventional and pleasing. And we close the album with"Animaemotica," another very cool electronic diversion that features Eva's dancing flute andBrozzetti's solo as the lead instruments over the somewhat somber background. Petrini's drumminggets heavier before Cecchini's wails and Eva's flute bring us into port. Seme is eclectic, immediate, and thoroughly enjoyable to my ear. I do believe this album willhave its detractors because of the break from their well-known sound of the trilogy, but I foundthis all refreshing and filled with absolutely invested performances. They sound energized to bepainting with some new colors, a vibe that would carry through to the excellent live performances onAnimAcusticA and the next studio album, Imilla. For a band that's been around andactive for nearly a quarter century to date, they remain as potent as ever in both songwriting andperformance. They are a treasure of Italian progressive rock.

items._cn_summary: 这是意大利前卫摇滚乐队第四张录音室专辑，评论者认为乐队在前三张专辑确立的声音基础上大幅拓宽了风格边界，将硬摇滚、民谣、融合、电子等元素融入以歌曲结构为主体的创作中。开场曲以混沌金属质感和愤怒的System of a Down式钩子建立冲击，随后转为意大利流行旋律的悠扬段落，紧接着是重型融合的狂飙段落。中段九分钟长曲以塔布拉鼓、慵懒萨克斯与原声吉他缓慢堆叠，构成专辑中段的喘息空间。电子鼓与合成器实验、短小的流行间奏、偏民谣化的收束段以及以长笛和吉他独奏主导的电子化终曲，共同构成一张风格碎片化、密度极高的作品。评论者明确表达了对这张偏离系列既定路线的专辑的强烈喜爱。

items.body: Review by Sean Trane — 3.5 stars reallyy!!Sole album from this late-60's outfit from Leuven that had a link with Shampoo, and it's a reallycollectible album, partly because of the musical quaintness on the black wax slice. Despitereleasing the album in 71, this is maybe a tad more 60's-ish , stuck between Auger's Trinity andearly Canterbury (IMHO). despite some local interest, they went pretty well unnoticed on theinternational scenes.The music is dominated by Wenstra's high-pitched vocals that can somehow make you think of SonjaChristina of Curved Air or Cos' Pascale Son (hence the Canterburt sonics). But the Hammond organ andsaxophone do give this fun jazz-rock, bordering brass-rock. All of the relatively short tracks aresongs that let some excellent musicanship and they peak with Music, The Reason of Our Happiness. Thealbum does somewhat well on the flipside, despite the awesome Jack Is Away and the following 5Longhaired Children in a Cave, but the closing instrumental is a bit of a down note (not reallyfitting what came before).One of those one-shot curio from Belgium that is worth the detour, but maybe not at all cost tobring it home.
items._genre: jazz rock / fusion / Canterbury-inspired / brass rock
items._cn_summary: 这是一张来自比利时鲁汶乐队的唯一专辑，1971年发行但风格更偏向六十年代末期。受Auger三重奏和早期坎特伯雷流派影响，作品以爵士摇滚为基底，融入管乐元素。主唱Wenstra的高音演唱令人联想到Curved Air的Sonja Christina和Cos的Pascale Son，营造出坎特伯雷式的声乐质感。Hammond管风琴与萨克斯的搭配赋予音乐活泼的爵士摇滚气质，间或触及铜管摇滚的边缘。专辑曲目普遍较短但结构完整，器乐演奏水平出色，高峰出现在Music, The Reason of Our Happiness一曲。B面整体表现稳定，Jack Is Away和5 Longhaired Children in a Cave尤为出色，结尾的器乐曲则略显突兀，与前文风格衔接不够自然。作为比利时音乐史上的罕见遗珠，这张专辑具有收藏价值。

items.body: Review by alainPP — "Cendo" stands out for its thunderous, Balkan-tinged folk-space sound, amplified by Alexander's accordion?a true virtuoso, it must be said; an easy-listening tune that invites daydreaming. "Issero" is ambient psychedelic from the outset; a track notable for the 'battle' between Alexander and Vladimir on their bewitching guitars over a cosmic flash. A heavy riff and the frenetic musical fire with the accordion induce a trance-like state, the mandolin not on MINIMUM VITAL but on a certain Greek island devoted to excess. Excess of notes scattered at will, imprinting a fresh new sound."Joreil" stands out for its acoustic guitar, its oriental folk atmosphere more than psychedelic. The gradual build-up with the accordion, the centerpiece of the tracks, before the jazz-rock guitar finale that levitates between two spheres, an innovative, melancholic, spacey outro. "Tio," for the vibrant guitar, I'll let the musician explain the technique; the atmosphere it creates leads us down a cloudy path, like raindrops gathering before falling. A moment of respite with the fruity guitar; I think of all those jazz-rock aces of the 70s who dared to unleash solos almost juicier and heavier than the guitar heroes; I think of John McLaughlin, Frank Gambale, and Al Di Meola. The finale with the musical rain now falling."Akkani" for a spacey bossa nova, a crescendo of sound from which the guitar carves its way across the stars. The accordion makes the piece warm, contemplative, radiant behind the folk guitar, the Balkans with this medieval setting suggested by the mandolin. "Plake" follows, same style, spacey sounds embellished with traditional instruments evoking the pacifist Great East. The wah-wah pedal is used to great effect, creating a hazy atmosphere for a while before plunging into a heavy, stressful, then frenetic sound."Capitli" shifts gears, a jazzy, barroom vibe with the sticky accordion clinging to the fleeting sound. The rich, viscous guitar hypnotizes the ear before the insidious break gently descends into melancholic turmoil. "Far" closes this unique album with an acoustic-electric duet of guitars gently juxtaposing, then frantically. Ivan on drums unleashes an explosion of the senses before giving way to the velvety guitars.VESPERO mixes everything together, adding a few spacey, psychedelic keyboards, and you have a fresh album to enjoy without moderation, far removed from the usual progressive conventions.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / space rock / world fusion / folk
items._cn_summary: 这是一张以迷幻和太空摇滚为骨架、融入巴尔干及东方民族元素的跨界专辑。乐评逐曲展开描述：手风琴作为核心乐器贯穿全作，与吉他形成张力十足的对话，营造出冥想般的恍惚氛围；民谣吉他段落提供喘息空间，带有爵士摇滚吉他英雄的影响；尾段以原声电声吉他二重奏收束，鼓手带来感官爆发的段落。制作上将传统乐器、迷幻键盘与空间音效混合，既不拘泥于常规的前摇滚框架，也保留了较强的旋律可听性。来自俄罗斯的VESPERO乐团将巴尔干民间音乐色彩与地中海岛屿气质注入迷幻摇滚结构中，整体呈现出一种独特的、介于民俗与太空之间的听觉体验。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — With an aesthetic reminiscent of A Clockwork Orange, it could be nothing other than the Canterbury scene transported to the Netherlands.That peaceful opening with the flute is interrupted by distinctly progressive tracks, which set them apart from pioneers like Soft Machine. Led by keyboards and heavily influenced by jazz, like Frank Zappa in his Hot Rats era.But it was more than just a collection of influences... there was something aggressive about this quartet, something unsettling. The piano possessed the modernity of the 60s masters, while the fuzz bass and drums, along with Robert Jan Stips' atonal vocals, imbued it with an unmistakable 70s aura.Memories Are New introduces a keyboard that distorts to the very edge of psychedelia, and since Marco Vrolijk was a drummer who mastered both the subtlety of jazz and the ethereal spirituality of Bossa Nova, he could perfectly complement these rhythmic shifts. 11/8 is unmistakably Soft Machine, and the keyboard's oscillations vibrate and mutate like a lamp whose energy is intermittent, illuminating at times and plunging everything into complete darkness at others. An electric guitar wasn't necessary when the distortion could come from the keyboard and the contrasts were layered with such audacity and speed. That's why it's an album that surprises, that takes you by surprise, subversive in many ways, just like the decade that saw its birth.At times they created cinematic atmospheres, as in "Dreaming Wheelwhile"... to denser offerings like "Mexico," with its oriental influences, accompanied by percussion, and an esoteric, almost revelatory haze... within reach... but evaporating like fog when the sun rises in the morning.A classic vocal section accompanied by keyboards, which then accelerates, introduces us to "Metamorphosis," a garage rock track with punk and acid krautrock influences... mechanically repetitive. "Dona Nobis Pacem" is like the calm after committing the crime...and new promises for the next chapter, which will not bring more of the same but new things from the same quartet.

items._cn_summary: Supersister将坎特伯雷场景移植到荷兰，以键盘为主导，融合爵士元素与七十年代的迷幻氛围。专辑开篇的横笛宁静旋即被锋利的不协和和声打断，罗伯特·扬·斯蒂普斯的无调性演唱配以失真贝斯和鼓击，赋予四重奏一种不安分的侵略性。Marco Vrolijk的鼓技横跨爵士的细腻与波萨诺瓦的空灵，在11/8拍这样的复合节奏中游刃有余。键盘的失真延伸至迷幻边界，振荡如接触不良的灯管明灭交替，替代了电吉他的角色。墨西哥一曲融入东方打击乐和密教般的低语雾气，蜕变一曲则滑向车库摇滚与酸涩的克拉夫特洛克脉冲。整体呈现出兼具电影画面感与机械重复性的怪诞美学。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — I have been a fan of Kristoffer Gildenl�w since the very early days of Pain of Salvation, since when he has undertaken an interesting musical career, working as a session musician as well as releasing solo albums, with this being his sixth. One of the joys of his albums is that one never knows quite what area he is going to explore and I was surprised to find him going back to his prog metal roots, throwing in elements of djent, mathcore, doom and more while always maintaining the progressive and commercial overtones which make him stand out. It is certainly a very different beast indeed to his last two releases, 'Let Me Be A Ghost' (2021) and 'Empty' (2024), and a welcome diversion.He of course provides most of the instruments himself but has wisely brought in a real drummer in Leo Margarit (Pain of Salvation, For All We Know) while two guests get a guitar solo each, Daniel Magdič (Prehistorical Animals, ex-Pain of Salvation), and Dutch guitarist Thijmen van der Meer. Somehow, Gildenl�w has managed to retain the huge soundscapes and emotions we expect from him, but has focussed much more strongly on the guitar, using different techniques and time signatures to ensure we never have too much time to rest and instead are always looking to hear what comes next and what is around the corner. Just when we think we have it all worked out he changes gear and switches to a different direction, going quiet when it seems we are heading to a climax, and then riffing hard when it appears to be heading to calm.The result is a thoroughly enjoyable and modern progressive rock album which touches on many different subgenres and is all the better for it.
items._genre: progressive metal / djent / mathcore / progressive rock
items._cn_summary: 这是Kristoffer Gildenlöw的第六张个人专辑，回归了他早年在Pain of Salvation时期的金属根源。专辑融合了djent、mathcore和doom等元素，同时保留了前卫与流行的质感，与前两张作品的氛围化方向形成鲜明对比。Gildenlöw亲自演奏了大部分乐器，并邀请了Pain of Salvation的鼓手Leo Margarit担任真实鼓手，另有两位客座吉他手分别贡献独奏段落。专辑在宏大的音景与情感表达之间保持平衡，吉他表现尤为突出，运用多样技巧与复杂节拍不断推进，频繁切换动态与方向，避免任何舒适区域。整体而言，这是一张融合多种前卫金属子风格的现代作品，在保持个人特色的同时拓宽了音乐边界。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — This is not the first time that Jordsj� and Breidablik have released an album together, as back in 2016 there was 'Songs From The Northern Wasteland', but that featured multiple songs from each band. This time around each band has a side to themselves for just one long piece, in each case titled "Kontraster". The other main difference between the two albums is that when the first was released, Breidablik was very much a solo project from keyboard player Morten Birkeland Nielsen, but in recent years he brought in firstly Hakon Oftung (guitar, flute) from Jordsj� to play on 2020's 'Omicron', and then drummer Trond Gjellum to also play on 2022's 'Alduorka' so it is this trio on Side B while Hakon also provides keyboards and vocals on Side A and is of course joined by drummer Kristian Frland. It was only recently that I raved over Jordsj�'s latest release, 'Pestkr�nikene', and yet again I find I am taken back in time to the heyday of commercial progressive rock and the early to mid-Seventies. It is relaxed, inviting, and again feels very analogue and one is never sure if we are going to spend more time in the realms of folk or symphonic, and while some could argue that it is all about Oftung and his skills as a multi-instrumentalist, the playing of Frland takes it to a whole new level and there are times when he remind me of Bill Bruford, at others Neal Peart. At 20 minutes in length I think this is the longest track recorded by the duo, and it will be interesting to see if they repeat the experiment as this if fascinating throughout and never overstays its welcome as it is comprised of so many individual sections.Even though Oftung plays on both sides, his role under Nielsen is very different indeed, as one would expect from working with an electronics wizard who has long been influenced by Tangerine Dream and for whom working on lengthy pieces is nothing new. Although I enjoy electronic music as much as the next proghead, for some reason I had not come across Breidablik prior to this joint release, but now I have I can see I am going to have to investigate further as this is highly polished and dramatic. Again, this never feels as if it is something modern but feels as if it is coming to us from the end of the Seventies when electronic bands were starting to make their presence felt and one can certainly imagine this forming part of a film soundtrack, especially if we were following reindeer in the snow across mountains and valleys. At least that is what I "see" while listening to this.Overall this is a great introduction to both bands and highly recommended for progheads who wish the last 50 years had not taken place.
items._genre: symphonic prog / electronic prog / retro prog
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由两支乐队各占一面，分别贡献一首同名长曲。Jordsjø 侧的多乐器演奏者 Oftung 联合鼓手 Frøland 呈现了接近七十年代商业前卫摇滚黄金时期的声音，融合民谣与交响元素，鼓手表现令人联想到 Bill Bruford 与 Neil Peart，整体松弛而具模拟质感。Breidablik 侧由键盘手 Nielsen 主导，受 Tangerine Dream 影响的电子乐风格被铺陈在二十多分钟的篇幅中，氛围浓重且具电影配乐感，描绘出雪地中驯鹿迁徙的北欧意象。两支乐队此前已有合作，本次的差异在于 Breidablik 已从单人项目扩展为三人编制，而整张专辑作为双方作品的合集，适合对复古前卫与电子融合感兴趣的乐迷作为入门。

items.body: Review by kev rowland — Here is the latest release from one of my favourite improvisational acts, �resund Space Collective, which this time around is a split album with Hungarian outfit Psychedelic Source Records who cite �SC as being one of their major influences. Side A is one long jam, "Zephyr In Orbit" and rarely feels improvised as �SC feel incredibly tight on this with Mattias and Jiri keeping the foundation soundly locked down, keyboard players Love and Dr. Space knowing when to provide background and when to drift to the fore and Jonathan often allowing his guitar to be strident and in your face. This must be one of the most connected pieces I have come across from these guys, and even though it is more than 21 minutes long it never feels as if it has overstayed its welcome and, in many ways, acts as a great introduction to the band if a listener has wondered where to start.Psychedelic Source Records is a new name to me, and it is obviously they are highly influenced by �SC but in some ways they are even more of a collective in that over the course of the three tracks no musician plays on more than two, and many play on just one, so over the two quartets and one trio featured over the three songs on Side B there are 9 different musicians, with no-one playing on more than one song with any other musician. One might think this would mean incredibly varied music, but the result never sounds as if it comes from different bands, as they have their spaced-out psychedelia firmly front of mind at all times. I know that if I had more time, I would investigate their catalogue as it is currently possible to purchase all 101 of their releases from Bandcamp for a total price of just ?1 or more, but I'll never get any more reviewing done if I succumb to that temptation.As it is, this release is a great introduction to two highly imaginative improvisational outfits, and is definitely worthy of investigation.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / space rock / improvisation / krautrock
items._cn_summary: 这是一张Split LP分辑专辑，A面由Öresund Space Collective带来21分钟的长篇即兴jam作品'Zephyr In Orbit'，乐队成员配合紧密，键盘与吉他层次清晰，既有低沉稳固的节奏根基，又有浮出表面的旋律线条，整体虽为即兴录制却结构感极强。B面由匈牙利乐队Psychedelic Source Records呈现三首曲目，其特色在于九位乐手中无人参与超过两首作品，但通过统一的空间迷幻美学保持了连贯风格。两支乐队均为注重即兴创作的集体，ÖSC是成熟的乐手组合，后者则更具开放性，成员流动频繁。整张专辑展示了欧洲地下即兴场景中迷幻/太空摇滚的活力，两组音乐人在不同时空中探索着相似的声响宇宙。

items._cn_summary: 南非钢琴家兼作曲家Nduduzo Makhathini同时身兼传统治疗师（sangoma），其音乐超越了单一时刻的声响，延续着某种永恒的精神脉络。专辑由Blue Note厂牌发行，融合了南非传统音乐根源与爵士语汇，探讨父子关系与神话的力量，将祖鲁文化中的精神性与现代爵士钢琴即兴结合。其创作植根于非洲大陆的传统信仰体系与世界音乐土壤，在Blue Note的框架下呈现出学院爵士的即兴深度与跨文化叙事。但因原文为新闻摘要式简介，内容极为简短，缺乏对实际音乐技法的具体描述，信息量不足以支撑深入评析，限制了对其创新性的判断深度。

items._cn_summary: 这张作品由Prism萨克斯四重奏与David Dzubinski合作，呈现一种介于当代室内乐与跨界实验之间的形态。演出于费城自由图书馆，邀来人声表演者Ursula Rucker、打击乐手Tyshawn Sorey及小提琴手Carlos Santiago共同参与编排与演绎，使原本的室内乐框架被扩展为人声、打击乐与弦乐的多层对话。曲目在不到四分钟内从粗粝走向抒情再返回，动态跨度大，兼顾细腻与张力。整体编排强调即兴互动与音色碰撞，既保留四重奏的学院根基，又融入自由爵士的开放语汇，对熟悉当代作曲与实验即兴交叉领域的听众具有吸引力。

items.body: Editor's note: When this set of recordings came to me, I was at a loss as to how to share it. It's not music, in any traditional sense (although there is some freestyle rapping), and a 'review' of such an artifact of reality seems superfluous to the content. Instead, I asked sound recordist Ian Brennan if I could simply use his own brief commentary and the recordings he made on the street in Chicago. Twenty-five people afflicted by gun violence participated, many from the very block we�d setup on. Many neighbors were pulled-in spontaneously. Almost every one in the community had been impacted by violence somehow� both on the receiving and the inflicting end, and many both. One woman had just come from a memorial service, another was on her way. That�s how far-reaching the violence. Almost no one went untouched. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors By chance, we convened on the day that Trump ordered the deployment of the National Guard to the city. The recording took place on the front porch of the leader's ninety-four-year-old grandmother's house�right in the heart of the ��hood,� beneath the Midway Airport�s landing path. A pair of stray pitfalls stalked the block. But the grandmother warned not of gunshots, but the mosquitoes in her yard. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors We were in a section of town that one man defined as �the forgotten parts.� Just a short jaunt from the designer clothes shops and posh hotels of the city�s Magnificent Mile, the Southside spawned such legendary Blues artists as Muddy Waters, Willie Dixon, and Howlin� Wolf. Jazz musicians like Lionel Hampton and even Benny Goodman, hailed from nearby. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors The participants ranged in age from seventeen to sixty-seven, but the pattern held true. The person who�d asserted �you�ll really want to hear my story,� was the least compelling. The reluctant, the most moving. One elder�s tough facade broke down as she shared how she�d lost both her sons. She tearfully apologized, �I�m sorry. I�m sorry. I�m sorry.� But she had nothing to be sorry for. Society is the one that owes the apology� for the staggering statistical inequities of which no reasonable defense can be made. The Forgotten Parts by Chicago Gunfire Survivors Editor's note: The full set of recordings are available on Bandcamp. Any profits from this project will be donated to Cure Violence Global , who states that their mission is "advancing an evidence-based health approach to end violence globally." When I asked him about the background sounds, producer Ian Brennan added, "No music is added. It�s all sounds from the source environment. I also ran loops/drones on a different track in the background as they spoke, and when they ended up being incidentally/somewhat magically/eerily synchronous, that is what was used for a few pieces with 'accompaniment' like some of the rap freestyles."
items._genre: field recording / spoken word / documentary / sound art
items._cn_summary: 这张作品并非传统意义上的音乐专辑，而是声音记录者Ian Brennan在芝加哥南区街头录制的枪支暴力幸存者口述合集。录制地点位于一位九十四岁老人家的前廊，恰逢特朗普下令国民警卫队进驻芝加哥之日。参与者年龄从十七岁到六十七岁不等，以即兴的方式讲述自己与暴力相关的亲身经历。一位失去两个儿子的老人在讲述过程中情感崩溃，反复道歉。编辑明确表示不添加任何音乐，呈现的完全是真实环境中的声音与话语。该项目具有一定的田野录音和声音艺术实验性质，超越了音乐评论的范畴，更接近社会纪实文献。收益将捐赠给反暴力公益组织。整体而言，作为声音艺术或社会声学作品具有独特视角，但对纯粹关注音乐性的听众而言，音乐价值有限。

items.body:
In 2026, I was invited to join the Silkroad Ensemble, the international collective directed by Rhiannon Giddens, as a musician (frame drums, violin, and voice) and contributor of new arrangements and compositions. Following an initial workshop and preview performance in New York in January 2026, the project will unfold through a North American tour in March 2026, featuring nine concerts alongside workshops and community outreach activities across the United States, as part of the new program
Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual
. The tour will continue later in the year with further residencies and performances in North America and Europe.
There are musical projects that are built around a repertoire, others around a geography, and others still around a specific aesthetic vision. The Silkroad Ensemble belongs to a different category: it is a living organism built around an idea. A simple and radical idea at once�that music can be a real space of encounter between cultures, not as a symbolic gesture, but as a daily, concrete, lived practice.
Founded in 1998 by Yo-Yo Ma, Silkroad has never been an ensemble in the traditional sense. There is no fixed lineup, no stable repertoire. Instead, it is a community of musicians from different traditions, chosen not only for their technical excellence, but for their ability to inhabit a threshold�the space between rootedness and transformation. Each musician brings with them a language, a sound, a memory. What matters most is the willingness to place that language in dialogue with others, without hierarchy.
In recent years, the project has been guided by Rhiannon Giddens, one of the most powerful and deeply insightful voices in contemporary music. Her presence gives the work a clear direction: the goal is not to create an artificial synthesis of traditions, but to create the conditions for each tradition to speak fully, and to transform through encounter. Rhiannon possesses a rare kind of leadership�one that never imposes itself, but quietly shapes the space, both musically and humanly.
Entering this context means immediately finding yourself in a space where musical identity is not something to defend, but something to offer. The pizzica, the frame drums, the violin I carry with me are no longer only instruments of a local tradition, but elements in a broader conversation, where every sound is heard both for what it is and for what it might become.
It is within this space that my participation in Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual began to take shape. Even before the music itself, what stands out is the quality of listening. A real, deep listening, in which every musical gesture is at once personal and collective. This, perhaps, is the true nature of Silkroad: not simply an ensemble, but a place. A circle. A space where music returns to what it has always been�a form of relationship.
Sanctuary: The Power of Resonance and Ritual
Music as Refuge and Resistance
The word sanctuary can be understood in many ways: refuge, protected space, a place where it is still possible to pause, to listen, to rebuild a sense of community.
Working on this project in the United States today carries a particular weight. This is a country marked by deep and increasingly visible tensions, where public discourse is often shaped by fear, by closure, by the idea that identity is something to be defended against someone else. The same tendency can be seen elsewhere�in Italy, across Europe, and in many parts of the world. The rise of nationalism, ongoing wars, and increasingly restrictive migration policies contribute to a climate in which separation begins to feel like the natural order of things.
Within this context, finding yourself in a room each day with musicians from Morocco, India, Japan, Armenia, Scotland, Congo, Italy, and the United States becomes something very real. Each person brings their own history, their own sound, their own way of inhabiting music. What emerges is not a fusion of identities, but their coexistence.
The taranta, Gnawa music, Indian classical tradition, American folk music�these practices were never conceived merely as forms of entertainment. They were born as tools to accompany moments of transformation, to help individuals and communities move through crisis, grief, healing, and renewal.
Sanctuary begins with this understanding. With the idea that music can still be a space where encounter is possible without the need to simplify or protect oneself. A space where listening becomes an act of trust.
Something simple and real happens: people from different parts of the world breathe together, listen together, and build something that did not exist before. In a time that often pushes toward division, this act acquires a different weight. It becomes, in its own quiet way, a form of resistance.
Entering the Circle
The first rehearsals are always a delicate moment. I took part in an initial workshop in Ireland last December, with a smaller group�Rhiannon, Mazz, Francesco, Niwel, and myself�and then a second workshop with the full ensemble in January, followed by a beautiful preview performance in New York on January 10, 2026, as part of the Winter Jazz Fest.
At that stage, there is no shared language yet. You observe each other, you play, you try things, you listen. What strikes you immediately is the extraordinary musical and human level of the people involved. They are incredible. Not only great instrumentalists, but musicians who have developed a deep relationship with their own musical traditions, and who have learned to question them, to keep them flexible and alive.
The Hawaiian bassist Shawn Conley, for example, moves effortlessly between bow and pizzicato, shifting from a lyrical, singing tone to remarkable rhythmic agility, using the instrument with a freedom that easily recalls the expressive range of a cello.
Beside him, Scottish harpist Maeve Gilchrist brings a presence that is both refined and fearless. Beyond a complete mastery of everything one might expect from the harp�the luminous, almost celestial sound�she possesses an extraordinary rhythmic and harmonic awareness, and a musical curiosity that allows her to make bold, unexpected choices without hesitation.
Armenian cellist Karen Ouzounian represents the very highest level of classical tradition, but with something more: a strong personal voice, a deep compositional sensibility, and a lyrical approach to improvisation that makes every gesture feel necessary.
With Francesco Turrisi, who like me comes from Italy, we already share a longer history. Yet I remain constantly struck by his ability to move between radically different instruments�accordion, piano, frame drums, string instruments�with complete naturalness. His immense musicality is not tied to any single instrument, but to a broader understanding of sound, form, and structure.
Congolese guitarist Niwel Tsumbu is simply one of the finest guitarists I have ever encountered. His relationship with the guitar transcends the instrument itself. He brings together a deep knowledge of African musical traditions, an innate rhythmic sensibility, refined harmonic awareness, and an extraordinary improvisational freedom.
Kaoru Watanabe embodies, in a profound way, the idea that tradition is also a choice. Japanese and American, he moves fluidly between cultural languages with a rare balance of respect, discipline, and expressive freedom. His playing is never a reproduction of the past, but its living continuation.
With Mehdi Nassouli, on guembri and voice, I feel a particular closeness. Like me with pizzica, he belongs deeply to a specific musical world�in his case, the Gnawa tradition of Morocco. Yet his experience has given him an equally deep ability to engage in dialogue with other musical languages, without ever losing the center of his own sound.
Sandeep Das�s presence on tabla is a constant point of reference. He is, quite literally, a guru of Indian music, and yet his authority never creates distance. On the contrary, he makes every interaction feel natural, effortless, both musically and humanly.
Japanese percussionist Haruka Fujii brings an extraordinary level of precision and listening. Her virtuosity is never displayed for its own sake, but always placed in service of the music, strengthening the cohesion of the ensemble.
American violinist and vocalist Mazz Swift embodies a rare combination of strength and openness. Their voice and violin move fluidly across genres and traditions, grounded yet constantly searching, expanding the expressive space of the group.
And then there is Rhiannon. It is difficult to find a single word that captures her presence. She is a complete musician�singer, instrumentalist, composer, dancer, and leader�but above all, she possesses a clarity of vision that holds everything together and inspires everyone around her. Her leadership does not operate through control, but through listening. She creates a space in which each musician can fully express themselves, while contributing to something larger than any individual voice.
Common Ground
"Common Ground" is the pizzica I wrote for the Silkroad Ensemble. I use the word �wrote� with caution, because the piece truly exists only through the creative contribution of each musician involved. I laid the foundations: the rhythm, the groove, the structure, the overall architecture, and the fixed melodic and harmonic elements. But what makes it alive is the way each musician inhabits it.
The idea first emerged during the workshop in Ireland. At that stage, we were still searching for common ground, a way of being together musically without renouncing our individual identities. It felt natural for me to bring the rhythm of pizzica�my familiar and chosen refuge, my Sanctuary.
Back home, I began to develop that intuition, shaping a structure that preserved the physical and rhythmic core of the tradition, while remaining open enough to allow each musician to find their own place within it. We worked on the piece during the workshop in the United States, and performed it live for the first time in New York, just days later, at the Winter Jazz Fest.
It was extraordinary to witness how naturally each musician entered that rhythm without hesitation. No one was trying to imitate something that did not belong to them. Instead, each voice emerged clearly, freely coexisting alongside the others.
In that moment, I understood that the piece had found its true meaning. It was no longer simply the pizzica I had written, but a shared space. A Common Ground laid beneath our feet.
Experiences like this change you in subtle but lasting ways. The energy they transmit, the enthusiasm, the renewed sense of trust in the future�all of it remains.
A few years ago, I was in Adelaide to perform at WOMAD with Justin Adams, and the night before our concert I had the chance to attend a performance by Billy Bragg. At one point, he said something that has stayed with me ever since: �Music does not have the power to change the world. But it can make you believe that the world can be changed.�

items._cn_summary: 这是西班牙吉他手Dani Janú的第三张专辑，融合弗拉门戈、加泰罗尼亚民间音乐、古典音乐、爵士及诗歌文本。专辑核心为吉他与长笛的对话，辅以循环音效、合成器、打击乐和人声，编制灵活。Janú毕业于巴塞罗那利塞欧高等音乐学院，兼具古典、弗拉门戈与爵士训练，并在多国深造。曲目中有向家族致敬的伦巴、为父母故居创作的米隆加、融入惠特曼诗句的古典组曲，以及受卡纳提克声乐打击乐影响的探戈-弗拉门戈作品。专辑代表新一代加泰罗尼亚学院派艺术家对弗拉门戈的开放态度，将其视为多元影响之一而非唯一根基。整体编曲细腻克制，融合层次丰富但偏向抒情化表达，实验性与前卫感有限。

items.body: Tovi by Teija Niku It�s been a lengthy wait for the fourth album from Finnish accordionist Teija Niku, but she�s hardly been idle over the last few years. Between the pandemic, giving birth, and the death of her mother, her time has been filled. But the long pause makes this return all the sweeter, with its joyful exploration of the places where the music of her homeland intersect with her deep love of Balkan music. Tovi by Teija Niku That�s amply illustrated on her composition �Finsko Dajchovo,� inspired by the Bulgarian folk dance rhythm, a loving creation that moves sprightly and gracefully, or �Seitsem�n,� taking its cue from Macedonian love songs. The bright, springlike melody, light, full of promise and hope could have been written for eager dancing feet. Everywhere, Niku displays her acute sense of melody. �Elokuu,� a celebration of the late summer lights of August, is a lilting, wistful piece, yet tinged with shades of melancholy for the winter to come, a masterful evocation of shifting moods. Tovi by Teija Niku While the influence of Balkan music hovers over Tovi (the title, according to Niku, translates as �an undefined bit of time, somewhere between a moment and a while�), a Nordic sensibility remains very much at its heart, with a couple of soaring polskas to move things briskly along, in a contrast to the brief, shadowy, brooding opener �Ohto.� Tovi by Teija Niku But the real heart of the disc comes at the very end, with �Poloneesi �idille,� a piece Niku composed for her mother�s 70th birthday, three years before she died. It�s a soft, elegiac work that suddenly becomes transcendent as she begins to sing, You can hear that this performance is completely from the heart, and it is a beautiful way to finish. Now to hope that it�s not such a long gap before she�s back in the studio. Find the artist online. Further listening: Duo Ruut - Ilmateade Maria Moramarco, Fabio Mina, and Francesco Savoretti - Pietrafonie Jaune Toujours - Vertigo

items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴演奏家Teija Niku暌违多年推出的第四张专辑，将北欧民俗音乐与巴尔干音乐传统相融合。专辑以保加利亚民间舞蹈节奏启发的《Finsko Dajchevo》为代表，旋律明亮轻快，充满春天的生机；《Elokuu》以悠扬而略带忧伤的笔触描绘八月暮夏的光影变幻，情绪层次丰富。专辑末尾的《Poloneesi Äidille》是Niku为母亲七十岁生日创作的挽歌之作，从柔和的哀悼逐渐升华为超脱的吟唱，真挚动人。整体展现出演奏家对旋律的敏锐把握与跨文化音乐语言的探索，专辑标题在芬兰语中意指介于'瞬间'与'一段时光'之间的模糊时段。

items.body: Echo by Emi Makabe L oss galvanizes, loss focuses, and musical artists turn loss into shared reflections. Emi Makabe has focused the passing of her father into a generous meditation on resilience and legacy with her second recording on Sunnyside Records, Echo . The title reminds us of the connections between generations. Here are ten musical memories that span time and culture, blending a modern jazz sensibility with a traditional Japanese soul. Born in Japan, where she studied Japanese traditional music, Emi Makabe moved to New York in 2008. She is an educator and contributor to the jazz scene, composing and performing her own music. Her previous recordings, an EP on the Japanese Jazz label D-Musica Out of Time (2016) and Anniversary (2020), laid the foundation of her sound: soaring, sweet singing in Japanese, English and wordless vocalizing, accompanied by her flute and shamisen on top of jazz-inspired piano, drums, and double bass. Using these materials, Makabe celebrates the legacy of her father, supported by Thomas Morgan (double bass, backing vocals) and Vitor Gon�alves (piano, accordion, Wurlitzer electric piano), both of whom return from her previous records, as well as Kenny Wollesen (drums, percussion, vibraphone, electronics). Also appearing as guests are Meshell Ndegeocello (spoken word), Jason Moran (piano), and Bill Frisell (acoustic guitar) on the opening track. Echo by Emi Makabe Opening with Frisell�s acoustic guitar and confidently sentimental, �Birthday Song� comes to grips with loss, featuring a touching spoken meditation and a haunting Frisell solo. It ends with the hope, �I wanna remember the warmth of being in your arms.� The record closes with �Overture,� anchored by Gon�alves� dripping Wurlitzer supporting Makabe�s Japanese exhortation, �Let's talk again, countless times/Let's talk, if we meet again.� Echo by Emi Makabe Besides the refreshingly unselfconscious sentimentality, Makabe strides confidently between the traditional Japanese melodies, instruments, and the language of her upbringing in her father�s world and the contemporary jazz of New York clubs. �Snow� begins with Makabe�s shamisen playing a pentatonic tune, while �Text� swings in a fast bebop, with Makabe�s flute and harmonized Japanese scat singing. Echo by Emi Makabe �Morisan� hurries between worlds led by bouncy accordion, rolling jazz traps, and a stylish piano solo by Jason Moran. Moran also shares production credits with Thomas Morgan and Makabe herself. Utterly unique in approach, and equipped with a lovely vocal instrument, and with a skilled and single-minded ensemble, Emi Makabe has created a passionate, introspective, and honest fusion of tradition and modernity to celebrate the passing of the generations. Find the artist online. Further listening: Carmen Souza - The Silver Messengers: A Tribute to Horace Silver Mamak Khadem - Rembrance Yussef Dayes - Black Classical Music
items.label: Sunnyside
items._cn_summary: Emi Makabe的第二张专辑以父亲离世为情感核心，将日本传统音乐与纽约当代爵士融合。十首作品横跨文化与时间，御笛、三味线、传统日本旋律与爵士钢琴、贝斯、鼓组展开对话。Bill Frisell的吉他开场，Jason Moran的钢琴独奏穿插其中，Meshell Ndegeocello贡献spoken word。专辑在日本语、英语与无词人声间自如切换，既有shamisen主导的五声音调，也有bebop节奏的flute独奏。制作团队由Thomas Morgan与Moran联合担任，整体呈现出真挚、内省且毫不造作的跨文化对话，将个人追思转化为对传承与韧性的音乐冥想。Sunnyside Records为独立厂牌。

items.body: Review by siLLy puPPy — First review of this album on PA!!! 70s prog season in Portugal was as short as summer in northern Scandinavia and just as soon as manyacts burst onto the scene, the sudden realization that the prog boom had subsided many years priorleft the recently liberated Iberian peninsula suddenly abandoning their prog complexities seeminglyas quickly as they developed them. ANANGA-RANGA is a somewhat obscure yet significant player in theworld of jazz fusion formed in Lisbon in 1976 and sticking it out until 1982. The band that featuredeight members cranked out a crafty fusion release "Regresso �s Origens" but quickly retreated afterthe commercial aspects of such music had since long passed. The band's followup PRIVADO immediately shifted gears and delivered a more sterile, less adventurousstyle that fused the band's clever fusion of symphonic prog and jazz rock into a easier listeningalbum of funk-fueled jazz rock and progressive pop.PRIVADO featured seven tracks which this timeadded vocal tracks that were geared towards the English speaking world, a trend that was way toocommon for once authentically pure bands that fused progressive rock into their homegrown musicalflavors. The results were that PRIVADO sounded like a completely different band than the debut with none ofthe crafty technical wizardry this time around but rather rather insipidly average song structuresthat occasionally hinted at the greatness that preceded but showcased a band clearly out of itselement grasping like a fish out of water to metabolize oxygen. The band now whittled down to fivemembers was a much more streamlined affair with less attention paid to crafty compositions andinstead attempted to nurture jazz fusion excursions into the context of progressive pop whichyielded diminishing results.The album opens with "Queen's Jail" which sounds more like The Doobie Brothers or some otherAmerican pop rock band of the 70s than the hypnotic fiery fusion that was inspired by the MahavishnuOrchestra and others. A clear pellmell to the sellout line, ANANGA-RANGA's sophomore release is arather mixed bag with the first four tracks struggling to pull out a pop hit before suddenly jumpinginto a more funk-fueled fusion style with "Estranha" which sounds more like a cheapened version ofHerbie Hancock or other funk fusionists of the 70s. While the debut stands as one of Portugal'sfinest progressive moments from the 1970s, PRIVADO stands as one of the most embarrassing displayinghow a highly talented band swapped out ardent ambition for commercial appeal but failed to scoreeither.Unlike fellow countrymen Tantra which delivered some of the best prog of the era and flawlesslytransitioned into a new wave band, ANANGA -RANGA on the other hand clumsily stumbled around lookingfor a way to remain relevant in a new musical reality that had come to dominate the world by theearly 80s. This album doesn't really know where it wants to go or what it's doing really. None ofthe tracks are downright horrible as much as they are totally uninspired and canned. In the end thealbum just sounds generic and ultimately a major disappointment for anyone expecting anothersizzling slab of Portuguese jazz fusion that sounded like no other. While i highly recommend thedebut, this one i can easily advise to give a miss.2.5 rounded down
items._genre: jazz rock / fusion / progressive pop / funk fusion
items._cn_summary: 这是一张1980年葡萄牙乐队ANANGA RANGA发行的第二张专辑，乐评对其评价颇为负面。乐评认为乐队首张专辑展现了受Mahavishnu Orchestra启发的精湛爵士融合技巧，而这张续作却大幅转向商业化方向，加入英语人声，试图在funk-fueled爵士摇滚与前卫流行之间寻找平衡。乐队成员从八人缩减至五人，编曲变得更为精简流畅，但失去了原有的技术复杂度和冒险精神。前四首曲目被描述为类似The Doobie Brothers的七十年代美式流行摇滚，缺乏首作的热烈与催眠感；第五首'Estranha'才回归funk融合路线，但被比作Herbie Hancock的廉价翻版。整体而言，乐评将此作视为一支有才华的乐队放弃艺术野心、追求商业却未能成功的尴尬过渡。
